title: QC-SVC-005 — Certificate of Origin Online
ac:
1. Frontend — Section 04: Documents Finder
User Story
As a public visitor preparing a
Certificate of Origin application,
I want to select my certificate
type, product type and export destination and immediately see which documents
Qatar Chamber requires for that exact combination,
So that I can gather the correct
paperwork before I start the application, instead of being rejected later for a
missing document.
Preconditions
- The Certificate of Origin Online page is published and
accessible in both English and Arabic.
- The Certificate type, Product type and Export
destination lookup lists are populated and active in the CMS.
- At least one active document-requirement entry exists in
the CMS.
- No login is required — the Documents Finder is fully
available to anonymous public visitors.
What the Visitor Sees
- A section eyebrow label reading “Prepare before
applying”, above the section heading “Required documents finder”.
- A short description: “Select your certificate format,
product category, and target export destination to view exact mandatory and
optional document specifications.”
- Three dropdown controls,: Certificate type (placeholder
“Select certificate type”), Product type (placeholder “Select product type”)
and Export destination (placeholder “Select export destination”).
- Before any selection is made, an empty-state helper
message in the results area: “Choose a certificate type, a product type and an
export destination to see the documents you need.”
- Once a selection is made, each applied selection
appears as a removable chip carrying the selected value and an × control — for
example “National export ×”, “Industrial products ×”, “GCC ×”.
- Below the chips, the matching document rows. Each row
shows a maroon circular document icon, the document title, a one-line
description beneath the title, and a right-aligned badge reading either
“Original” or “Certified Copy”.
- The sticky section index on the page shows four
entries: 01, 02, 03 and the new 04 Documents Finder. Selecting 04 scrolls the
page to this section; the index highlights 04 as the active entry while the
section is in view.
Frontend Workflow
- The visitor reaches the Certificate of Origin Online
page and scrolls to the Documents Finder section.
- The results area shows the empty-state helper message.
No document rows are displayed.
- The visitor opens any one of the three dropdowns. The
dropdown lists the active values for that lookup, in the CMS-defined display
order, in the current site language.
- The visitor selects a value. The dropdown closes, its
label is replaced by the selected value, a chip for that selection appears in
the chip row, and the results area immediately refreshes to show every active document
required for that selection.
- The visitor optionally selects a value in a second and
a third dropdown. Each additional selection narrows the result list further —
the finder returns only the documents required for that combined selection.
- The visitor can change any selection at any time by
reopening that dropdown and choosing a different value. The chip for that
dropdown is replaced, and the results refresh.
- The visitor can remove a selection by clicking the × on
its chip. The chip disappears, the dropdown returns to its placeholder, and the
results broaden again to reflect the remaining selections.
- If every chip is removed, the results area returns to
the empty-state helper message.
- If a combination has no matching documents configured,
the results area shows the no-results message instead of any rows.
- The visitor reads the document list and proceeds —
unchanged from the implemented story — to the Apply call to action elsewhere on
the page.
Acceptance Criteria
1.1 Section placement and index
Given
the Certificate of Origin Online page is published
When
the visitor loads the page
Then
the Documents Finder appears as the fourth section of the page and
the sticky section index displays four entries, 01 through 04, with the fourth
labelled “Documents Finder”
Given
the visitor is viewing the Certificate of Origin Online page
When
the visitor clicks the “04 Documents Finder” entry in the sticky
index
Then
the page scrolls to the Documents Finder section and the index
highlights 04 as the active entry
1.2 Empty state
Given
the visitor has made no selection in any of the three dropdowns
When
the visitor views the Documents Finder
Then
the results area displays “Choose a certificate type, a product type
and an export destination to see the documents you need.”, no chips are shown,
and no document rows are rendered
1.3 Single-selection filtering
Given
the visitor has made no selection
When
the visitor selects a Certificate type — for example “National
export”
Then
a chip reading “National export ×” appears, and the results area
lists every active document configured as required for that certificate type
Given
the visitor has made no selection
When
the visitor selects only a Product type, or only an Export
destination
Then
the finder filters on that single selection alone and returns the
documents required for it — a selection in all three dropdowns is not required
for results to be shown
1.4 Combined filtering
Given
the visitor has already selected a Certificate type and results are
displayed
When
the visitor additionally selects a Product type
Then
the result list is narrowed to only those documents required for
that certificate type and that product type together, and a second chip appears
Given
the visitor has selected a Certificate type and a Product type
When
the visitor additionally selects an Export destination
Then
the result list is narrowed to the documents required for all three
selections together, and three chips are displayed
Given
the visitor has a selection applied in one of the dropdowns
When
the visitor reopens that same dropdown and chooses a different value
Then
the previous selection is replaced rather than added, the chip for
that dropdown updates to the new value, and the results refresh against the new
combination
1.5 Chip removal
Given
three chips are displayed and the result list is filtered on all
three selections
When
the visitor clicks the × on one chip
Then
that chip is removed, its dropdown returns to its placeholder text,
and the result list broadens to the documents required for the two remaining
selections
Given
one chip remains and results are displayed
When
the visitor clicks the × on that last chip
Then
all three dropdowns show their placeholders and the results area
returns to the empty-state helper message
1.6 No results
Given
the visitor has applied a combination of selections for which no
active document requirement is configured in the CMS
When
the results area refreshes
Then
a no-results message is displayed — “No document requirements are
configured for this selection. Please contact Qatar Chamber for guidance.” —
the applied chips remain visible, and no document rows are rendered
1.7 Result row content
Given
document rows are displayed
When
the visitor reads a row
Then
the row shows a document icon, the document title, the document
description beneath the title, and a right-aligned badge reading either
“Original” or “Certified Copy” exactly as configured in the CMS
Given
document rows are displayed
When
the visitor attempts to interact with a row
Then
no row is clickable, no file is offered for download, and no upload
control is present — the rows are informational text only
Given
several documents match the applied selection
When
the results are rendered
Then
the documents appear in the display order configured in the CMS, and
a document that is configured for more than one of the applied selections
appears only once
1.8 Language and responsiveness
Given
the visitor is browsing the site in Arabic
When
the visitor uses the Documents Finder
Then
the section heading, description, dropdown labels, placeholders,
lookup values, chips, document titles, descriptions, badges and all state
messages are displayed in Arabic, with correct right-to-left layout and the
chip × control mirrored to the correct side
Edge Cases
- A document entry is deactivated in the CMS — it is
excluded from all results immediately, without affecting the other documents
matched by the same selection.
- A document is mapped to several certificate types,
product types or destinations — it is returned for each of them, but is never
shown twice within a single result list.
Post-condition
The visitor has seen the exact
list of documents Qatar Chamber requires for their stated certificate type,
product type and export destination. Nothing is submitted, stored or recorded
against the visitor — the Documents Finder is a read-only, stateless lookup,
and no application record is created by using it.
2. Backend — CMS Management of the Documents Finder
User Story
As a Qatar Chamber CMS
administrator,
I want to maintain the three
filter lists and the document requirements mapped against them,
So that the Documents Finder
always reflects the current Certificate of Origin requirements without any
redevelopment.
Preconditions
- The administrator is authenticated in the CMS.
- The Documents Finder content structures are deployed.
Administrator Workflow
- The administrator opens the Documents Finder area in
the CMS.
- The administrator maintains the three lookup lists —
Certificate Type, Product Type and Export Destination — adding, renaming,
reordering or deactivating values in English and Arabic.
- The administrator creates a document requirement,
entering its title, description and badge (Original or Certified Copy) in
English and Arabic and setting its display order.
- The administrator maps the document requirement to the
certificate types, product types and export destinations for which it is
required. A document can be mapped to one, several or all values in each list.
- The administrator saves the entry and it enters the
standard content lifecycle.
- The administrator can deactivate a document requirement
or a lookup value at any time; it is removed from the public finder immediately
on the next request, and historical content is unaffected.
Acceptance Criteria
Given
the administrator is maintaining the Documents Finder
When
the administrator adds, renames, reorders or deactivates a value in
any of the three lookup lists
Then
the change is reflected in the corresponding public dropdown without
any code change or deployment
Given
the administrator is creating a document requirement
When
the administrator saves it
Then
the entry cannot be saved and an inline validation message
identifies the missing mandatory field
Given
the administrator is creating a document requirement
When
the administrator saves it without mapping it to at least one value
in at least one of the three lookups
Then
the entry cannot be saved, because a document that is mapped to
nothing can never be returned by the finder
Given
a published document requirement exists
When
the administrator deactivates or unpublishes it
Then
it stops appearing in every public result list immediately, and all
other documents matched by the same selection continue to be returned
Given
an administrator performs any create, edit, deactivate or delete
action in this area
When
the action is saved
Then
the action is audit-logged with the acting user and timestamp, and
the standard CMS success toast is displayed, in line with the project's content
management lifecycle

4. Business Rules
- The Documents Finder is informational only. It displays
which documents are required for a selection — nothing more. No application is
started, no record is created, and no data about the visitor is stored.
- The section contains text only. No document entry
carries a file on the backend, and nothing is downloadable or unloadable on the
frontend.
- Filtering is progressive. Any single selection already
filters the results; two or three selections are combined, each one narrowing
the list further.
- Each dropdown holds a single selection. Choosing a new
value in a dropdown replaces the previous one rather than adding to it.
- Only active, published lookup values are offered in the
dropdowns, and only active, published document requirements are returned in the
results.
- A document mapped to more than one of the applied
selections is returned once, never duplicated within a result list.
- Result order is driven by the CMS display order, with
alphabetical title order as the tie-break. The visitor cannot re-sort the list.
- A combination with no configured documents returns the
no-results message, never a blank area or an error.
- Selections are not persisted — every page load starts
the finder in its empty state.
- The three lookup lists and the document requirements
are fully CMS-managed; adding, renaming, reordering or deactivating any of them
requires no redevelopment.
- Content is bilingual (EN/AR) with correct RTL support;
- All administrator actions respect RBAC, follow the content
management lifecycle, and are audit-logged.
- The Documents Finder is available to anonymous public
visitors; no login is required.
description:
1.
FRONTEND — Visitor Display
User Story
ID: QC-ESVC-005 | US-001 REF: FR-022
Title: Certificate
of Origin Online — Visitor Display
As a public website visitor
I want to open the Certificate of Origin
Online page, review the overview, read the required documents, follow the
how-to-apply steps, download the application form / compliance guide, and use
the Login to COO and Verify Certificate actions
So that I understand the COO service and
redirected to the official portal to apply or verify a certificate.
Preconditions
- The Qatar Chamber website is published and accessible.
- The Certificate of Origin Online page and its sections
are published in the CMS.
What the Visitor Sees
- Breadcrumb (Home › Services) and a hero with eyebrow,
title, description and two CTAs (Login to COO, Verify Certificate).
- A quick-facts strip (Service Channel, Certificate
Types, Verification, Coverage).
- A sticky numbered section index (01–03).
- Section 01 Overview — rich text plus three info cards
(Apply for a Certificate, Certificate Verification, Application Requirements).
- Section 02 Documents Required — a “Certificate of
Origin (PDF)” action button, an intro, and accordion document-requirement items
(e.g., “Certificate of Origin for Personal Effects”) that expand to show their
required-document lists.
- Section 03 How to Apply — an intro, a numbered 6-step
process, and a “Download the Application Form” card.
- A closing “Ready to continue” banner repeating Login to
COO and Verify Certificate, and the footer.
Frontend Workflow
- Visitor
navigates to Main Menu → Services → Certificate of Origin Online.
- The
page loads: breadcrumb, hero + two CTAs, quick-facts strip, sticky section
index, and all published sections in order.
- Visitor
reads the Overview and info cards.
- In
Documents Required, the visitor clicks a document-requirement item to expand
its content, and may click the “Certificate of Origin (PDF)” button to
open/download the compliance guide.
- In
How to Apply, the visitor follows the numbered steps and clicks Download on the
“Download the Application Form” card.
- Visitor
clicks Login to COO or Verify Certificate (hero or banner(ready to continue));
the system reads the configured redirect URL and opens the official platform in
the configured tab behavior.
Acceptance Criteria
Layout & rendering
Given the visitor opens the COO page
When the page renders
Then the system shall display the breadcrumb,
hero (eyebrow, title, description, both CTAs), the quick-facts strip, the
sticky section index, and all published sections in the configured display
order.
Section content
Given the Overview section is published
When it renders
Then rich text shall support headings,
paragraphs, bullets and inline hyperlinks, and each active info card shall show
its icon, title and description in order.
Given the Documents Required section is
published
When the visitor clicks a document-requirement
item
Then the item shall expand to show its
subtitle and required-document content, and collapse on a second click, without
a page reload.
Given the Documents Required PDF button is
configured
When the visitor clicks it
Then the system shall open/serve the
configured compliance-guide PDF (download or configured link).
Given the How to Apply section is published
When it renders
Then each active step shall display its
number, title and description in the configured order, and the “Download the
Application Form” card shall serve the configured file when clicked.
CTAs & redirects
Given a hero/banner CTA (Login to COO / Verify
Certificate) is active
When the visitor clicks it
Then the system shall redirect to the
configured official platform URL in the configured tab behavior (same/new tab).
Given a CTA is inactive/hidden by the CMS
When the page renders
Then that CTA shall not be displayed.
Bilingual, responsive
& governance
Given the visitor toggles language (EN/AR)
When the page renders
Then all labels, section content, cards,
steps, document-requirement items and CTA labels shall display in the selected
language with correct LTR (EN) / RTL (AR) layout.
Given the page is opened on desktop, tablet or
mobile
When it renders
Then the layout shall be responsive and
Given content is draft/unpublished or a
section/item is inactive
When the page renders
Then that content shall not appear on the
website.
Edge Cases
- If the selected-language translation is missing, the
section falls back to the (default language).
Negative Scenarios
- Draft or unpublished content (page, section, card,
document-requirement item, step, or download) shall not appear on the website.
Post Condition
The visitor has
read the COO information and required documents, followed the how-to-apply
steps, downloaded the application form / compliance guide, and is redirected to
the official COO or verification platform via the CTAs.
2.
BACKEND — Admin CMS Management
User Story
ID: QC-ESVC-005 | US-002 REF: FR-022
Title: Certificate
of Origin Online — CMS Management
As an authorized admin user (Site Content
Editor / Site Content Author)
I want to manage the COO page — hero + two
CTAs, quick-facts, Overview + info cards, Documents Required (PDF button +
accordion items), How to Apply (steps + application-form download), and the
next-step banner
So that visitors see accurate, ordered,
bilingual COO information and are correctly redirected to the official
platform.
Administrator Workflow
- Admin logs into Liferay CMS and navigates to E-Services
→ Certificate of Origin Online.
- Edits the hero: eyebrow, title (EN/AR), description
(EN/AR, rich text) and hero image.
- Configures the two CTAs (Login to COO, Verify
Certificate): label EN/AR, redirect URL, open behavior, active status — shared
by hero and next-step banner.
- Manages the quick-facts strip and the section index
(badge/title/order/active).
- Edits Overview body (EN/AR) and info cards (icon, title
EN/AR, description EN/AR, order, active).
- Manages Documents Required: sets the “Certificate of
Origin (PDF)” action button (label + file/URL + behavior), the intro, and the
accordion document-requirement items (title EN/AR, subtitle EN/AR, content
EN/AR, order, active).
- Manages How to Apply: intro, numbered steps (number,
title EN/AR, description EN/AR, order, active), and the “Download the
Application Form” card (title/subtitle EN/AR, file, label, active).
- Edits the next-step banner (eyebrow, heading, body).
- Saves as draft, previews, then publishes where
permitted.
- System validates content and URLs, refreshes cache,
records audit logs, and shows the Liferay generic success toast (EN/AR).
Acceptance Criteria
Given the admin manages the COO page
When the admin saves and publishes
Then the system shall allow create, edit,
preview, publish and unpublish for the page and every section/component where
permitted.
Given the admin manages repeatable items
(facts, info cards, document-requirement items, steps)
When the admin saves
Then each item shall support add, edit,
delete/deactivate, reorder and active/inactive toggle; only active, published
items shall appear in order.
Given the admin edits a CTA (Login to COO /
Verify Certificate)
When the admin publishes
Then the label shall update in EN and AR on
hero and banner, and each active CTA’s redirect URL shall be validated as a
valid URL before publishing.
Given the admin configures a download
(Compliance-guide PDF or Application Form)
When the admin publishes
Then the file/URL shall be validated (allowed
type/size or valid URL) and served on the frontend.
Given a document-requirement item is created
When the admin saves
Then each item shall require at least a title
and a content block; each content section shall require a title and content.
Given a mandatory bilingual field is missing
its Arabic value
When the admin publishes with Arabic enabled
Then publishing shall be blocked with a
validation message.
Given any change is made
When the admin acts
Then the system shall display the Liferay
generic success toast, record the change in the audit log, and support the
draft → preview → publish → unpublish lifecycle.
Negative Scenarios
- Uploading a download of a disallowed type or over the
size limit shall be blocked.

4.
Permissions
Role
Capabilities
Site Content Editor (Site Role)
Create, edit, view, preview, publish, unpublish the page,
all sections and repeatable items (facts, CTAs, info cards,
document-requirement items, steps, downloads) where permitted.
Site Content Author (Site Role)
View and update assigned page/section content where
permitted;
Public Visitor
View published content, expand document-requirement items,
download the compliance guide / application form, and use the Login to COO /
Verify Certificate redirects.
5.
Business Rules
- COO Online is a single consolidated informational page;
the actions are the Login to COO and Verify Certificate redirect CTAs (hero +
next-step banner).
- Only published, active content appears on the website,
in the configured display order.
- Both CTAs are configured once and reused by the hero
and the banner.
- All bilingual mandatory fields require Arabic values
when Arabic is enabled; layout must honor LTR (EN) / RTL (AR).
- All create/edit/publish/unpublish actions are recorded
in the audit log; each action shows the Liferay generic success toast.
